<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="center"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">PART I</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM </font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 13pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">1</font>.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">&#160;&#160;&#160;BUSINESS</font></font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac Corporation (&#8220;Innotrac&#8221; or the &#8220;Company&#8221;), founded in 1984 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, is an e-commerce provider integrating digital technology, order processing, fulfillment and customer support &#8220;contact&#8221; center services to support global brands of large corporations that outsource these functions.&#160;&#160;In order to perform these functions in-house, a company may be required to develop expensive, labor-intensive infrastructures, which may divert its resources and management&#8217;s focus from its principal or core business. By assuming responsibility for these tasks, Innotrac strives to improve the quality of the non-core operations of our clients and to reduce their overall operating costs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac receives most of our clients&#8217; orders either through inbound contact center services, electronic data interchange (&#8220;EDI&#8221;) or the internet.&#160;&#160;On a same day basis, depending on product availability, the Company picks, packs, verifies and ships the item, tracks inventory levels through an automated, integrated perpetual inventory system, warehouses data and handles customer support inquiries.&#160;&#160;Our fulfillment and customer support services interrelate and are sold as a package, however they are individually priced.&#160;&#160;Our clients may utilize our fulfillment services, our customer support services, or both, depending on their individual needs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">With facilities in Atlanta, Georgia, Pueblo, Colorado, Reno, Nevada, Bolingbrook, Illinois, Columbus, Ohio, two facilities in Hebron, Kentucky and a facility in Groveport, Ohio, we offer a national footprint to our customers.&#160;&#160;We are committed to deeper penetration within our existing business lines and continued diversification of our client base.&#160;&#160;Our long-term goal is to focus on current market growth trends while spreading our business across a higher number of clients in diverse industries to provide stability during difficult economic periods and avoid the risks associated with high individual account concentration and seasonality. We will continue to seek new clients and may open additional facilities as needed to service our customers&#8217; business needs.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fulfillment Services</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Providing effective turnkey order fulfillment solutions for our clients&#8217; products is our primary business.&#160;&#160;Our capabilities in this area are described below:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Fulfillment</font><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">.</font></font>&#160;&#160;We are committed to delivering our clients&#8217; products to their customers on a timely and accurate basis.&#160;&#160;Our personnel pick, pack, verify and ship product orders and requests for, shoes, clothing, electronic equipment, accessories, books, small appliances, home accessories, sporting goods and toys for our clients.&#160;&#160;We use several custom-designed, semi-automated packaging and labeling lines to pack and ship products as well as highly automated and conveyorized systems utilizing radio frequency (&#8220;RF&#8221;) scanning. By utilizing these technologies, we are able to reduce labor costs and provide more timely shipments to our clients&#8217; customers.&#160;&#160;We streamline and customize the fulfillment procedures for each client based upon the client request and the tracking, reporting and inventory controls necessary to implement that client&#8217;s marketing support program.&#160;&#160;We also offer comprehensive product return services whereby our personnel receive, log, test, repackage and dispose of products that are returned from end-users.&#160;&#160;Recognizing the importance of the total eCommerce buying experience to our customers, our SmartHub market surveys capture the competitive differences between eCommerce transactions tracking the start of order entry by the end consumer through speed and quality of shipment and ultimately the return process.&#160;&#160;Innotrac&#8217;s accuracy and speed of order processing is compared against same product category performance for our customers on an ongoing basis.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our operating locations have earned ISO 9001:2000 certification as follows: Atlanta in 2002 and again in 2010 after moving our fulfillment operations to a different facility, our first Hebron, Kentucky location in 2003, Pueblo in 2004, Chicago in 2005, Reno in 2006, our second Hebron, Kentucky location in 2008, and our Columbus location in 2009.&#160;&#160;&#160;All of our facilities other than Groveport, which was recently opened and scheduled for certification in -September of 2013, were re-certified to the ISO 9001-2008 revision of the standard in 2011.&#160;&#160;It is our intention to renew our current certificate upon its renewal date of December 20, 2014.&#160;&#160;We are dedicated to providing quality service to our clients at every step in the fulfillment process.&#160;&#160;To ensure order accuracy, shipment inspection and system driven validation are performed to verify the contents exactly match the order prior to shipment.&#160;&#160;In addition, we have highly sensitive scales at the end of our packaging lines that also assist in ensuring the accuracy of every order.&#160;&#160;Our 2012 order accuracy rate was 99.25%.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Inventory Management</font>.</font>&#160;&#160;An integral part of our fulfillment services is the monitoring and control of our clients&#8217; inventories.&#160;&#160;We provide automated inventory management and reporting to assure real-time stock counts of our client&#8217;s products, literature and other items.&#160;&#160;Our inventory systems enable us to provide management information to maintain consistent and timely reorder levels and supply capabilities and also enable the client to quickly assess stock balances, pricing information, reorder levels and inventory values.&#160;&#160;We offer this information to the client on a real-time basis through our internet gateway or direct system integration. Inventory management data is also utilized in our reporting services.&#160;&#160;We utilize bar coding equipment in our inventory management systems, which improves the efficiency of stock management and selection.&#160;&#160;We also perform cycle counts throughout the year to check system-maintained item balances against physical item balances.&#160;&#160;Our facilities have several layers of security.&#160;&#160;When necessary, we dispose of clients&#8217; products utilizing established guidelines.&#160;&#160;Disposal procedures vary depending on the product and client business rules.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Purchasing Management</font>.</font>&#160;&#160;For certain clients, we place orders for products we fulfill with vendors chosen by those clients.&#160;&#160;Our purchasing management services include assisting a client in negotiating product pricing with the vendor, arranging returns and credits as well as forecasting product quantities required for normal business programs or promotions.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Product Consignment and Warehousing</font>.&#160;&#160;For substantially all of our clients, we warehouse products on a consignment basis and fulfill orders on behalf of our customers for a fee.</font></font></div>

</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Contact Center Services</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Another of our core competencies is providing customer order and inquiry support services &#8211; Contact Center Services.&#160;&#160;We believe these services are critical to a comprehensive order processing and order fulfillment solution.&#160;&#160;Our Contact Center Services are described below.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Inbound Customer Support Services</font>.</font>&#160;&#160;Our customer service representatives take orders for certain clients and resolve questions regarding shipping, billing and order status as well as a variety of other questions.&#160;&#160;From time to time they may sell various products for our clients when end consumers call our customer service representatives.&#160;&#160;Depending on our client&#8217;s requirements, our customer service representatives use our internally developed customer relationship management system or through integrated technology portals, access client directed customer relationship information systems.&#160;&#160;To properly handle the call, Innotrac&#8217;s automated call distributor identifies each inbound call by the toll-free number dialed and immediately routes the call to the interactive voice response (&#8220;IVR&#8221;) system or an Innotrac customer service representative.&#160;&#160;If the caller is placing an order, the caller is immediately transmitted to a customer service representative trained to take the order and enter it into our systems for transmittal to the appropriate fulfillment center.&#160;&#160;If the customer has a question, complaint or needs return information, the IVR system attempts to resolve these issues by guiding the customer through a series of interactive questions. If IVR automatic resolution cannot solve the problem, the call is routed to one of our customer service representatives who answers the call using our client&#8217;s name and is specially trained in the applicable client&#8217;s business and products.&#160;&#160;Our customer service representatives can enter customer information into our call-tracking system, listen to a question and quickly access a proprietary network database using a graphical interface to answer a customer&#8217;s question.&#160;&#160;A senior representative is available to provide additional assistance for complex or unique customer questions.&#160;&#160;Customer service representatives are also trained to handle introductory level technical support issues.&#160;&#160;Customer requests are generally resolved with a single call, whether answered by a trained representative or our automated systems.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Returns and Refunds Processing</font>.&#160;&#160;The representatives respond to customer calls about product returns and refunds and obtain information about customer service problems.&#160;&#160;They facilitate a customer&#8217;s return of a product by providing a bar-coded label to the customer.&#160;&#160;When the returned item is processed and entered into our system, it automatically triggers a pre-set action for reshipment of a product or refund to the customer.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Technology</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our use of technology enables us to design and deliver services for each client&#8217;s fulfillment and customer support needs. Our information technology group, or IT Group, has developed our database marketing support and management systems.&#160;&#160;Innotrac has a technical integration platform based on a Webmethods core written in Java over an Oracle database, which contains a complete web interface using XML-based Advanced Programming Interface tools that allows clients to transact with us electronically.&#160;&#160;We deploy the solution running on HP enterprise class servers in a virtualized configuration running behind F-5 load balancers. Virtualization provides systems redundancy as well as rapid scalability.&#160;&#160;Oracle RAC (Redundant Application Cluster) is used for OLTP (Online Transaction Procession) and business intelligence databases.&#160;&#160;NetApp SAN (Storage Area Network) provides rapid access to data and the ability to scale data storage quickly depending on business demands.&#160;&#160;Network topology is a meshed MPLS (Multi Protocol Label Switching) architecture for primary data connectivity and DIA internet circuits utilizing VPN tunnels for secondary data access.&#160;&#160;Our burstable bandwidth allows us to quickly increase network bandwidth capacity.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The open architecture of our computer system permits us to seamlessly interact with many different types of client systems.&#160;&#160;Our IT Group uses this platform to design and implement application software for each client&#8217;s program, allowing clients to review their programs&#8217; progress on-line to obtain real-time comprehensive trend analysis, inventory levels and order status and to instantly alter certain program parameters.&#160;&#160;As the needs of a client evolve, our IT Group works with our client services team to modify the program on an ongoing basis.&#160;&#160;Information can be exchanged via real-time XML, direct system integration, EDI, secure FTP and internet access.&#160;&#160;We believe that our technology platform provides us with the resources to continue to offer leading edge services to current and new clients and to integrate our systems with theirs based on the clients preferred technology.&#160;&#160;We believe that the integrity of client information is adequately protected by our data security system and our off-site disaster back-up facilities.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We primarily utilize the WMOS system from Manhattan Associates as our warehouse management system.&#160;&#160;We use an internally-developed customized order management system (&#8220;OMS&#8221;) for clients at our various facilities.&#160;&#160;WMOS is an advanced fulfillment warehouse management system designed to support large volumes of transactions and users, which enables the effective management of high levels of throughput, from receiving through shipping.&#160;&#160;WMOS provides efficiencies in inventory management, outbound distribution and task management. Innotrac also offers a fully integrated direct marketing solution with a customized warehouse management system, front-end customer relationship management capabilities and a robust integration layer.&#160;&#160;Innotrac is also integrated with all the major ecommerce platforms such as Micros Retail, DemandWare, ATG and Magento.&#160;&#160;All of Innotrac&#8217;s solutions are PCI / DSS Level 1 compliant.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our Pueblo call center utilizes the Aspect Rockwell Spectrum Automatic Call Distributor, or ACD, switch to handle call management functions.&#160;&#160;The ACD system has the capacity to handle 1,200 call center representatives and as of December 31, 2012 was supporting<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</font>a capacity ranging from 200 to 450 representatives depending on our clients requirements.&#160;&#160;Additionally, the ACD system is integrated with workforce management software designed to enable management to staff and supervise the call center based on call length and call volume.&#160;&#160;Aspect&#8217;s AQM application is used for call monitoring and quality management.&#160;&#160;Customer service representatives enter orders received via telephone into our proprietary CRM application which is integrated with our order management and warehouse management systems.&#160;&#160;These orders are processed &#8220;real time&#8221; into one of our eight distribution centers.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Personnel and Training</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our success in recruiting, hiring and training large numbers of employees and obtaining large numbers of hourly employees during peak periods for fulfillment and contact center operations is critical to our ability to provide high quality fulfillment and customer support services.&#160;&#160;Contact center representatives and fulfillment personnel receive feedback on their performance on a regular basis and, as appropriate, are recognized for superior performance. Additional training is provided to all fulfillment center employees quarterly and to our call center representatives on an as-needed basis.&#160;&#160;To maintain good employee relations and to minimize employee turnover, we offer competitive pay and hire primarily full-time employees who are eligible to receive a full range of employee benefits.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As of March 1, 2013, we had approximately 1,450 full-time employees supported by temporary staff on an as-needed basis.&#160;&#160;Management believes that the demographics surrounding our facilities and our reputation, stability, compensation and benefit plans should allow us to continue to attract and retain qualified employees.&#160;&#160;Currently, we are not a party to any collective bargaining agreements.&#160;&#160;None of our employees are unionized.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Competition</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">In tailoring services to client needs, we compete on the basis of quality, reliability of service, scope of locations, efficiency, technical capabilities, speed and price.&#160;&#160;We compete with many companies, some of which have greater resources than we do with respect to various portions of our business.&#160;&#160;Those companies include fulfillment businesses and call center operations.&#160;&#160;We believe that our comprehensive and integrated services differentiate us from many of those competitors.&#160;&#160;We continuously explore new outsourcing service opportunities, typically in circumstances where clients are experiencing inefficiencies in non-core areas of their businesses and management believes we can develop a superior outsourced solution on a cost-effective basis.&#160;&#160;We primarily compete with the in-house operations of our current and potential clients and also compete with certain companies that provide similar services on an outsourced basis.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Government Regulation</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Telephone sales practices are regulated at both the federal and state level.&#160;&#160;These regulations primarily relate to outbound teleservices, which, in most cases, we outsource to another company.&#160;&#160;The few cases where we do conduct outbound teleservices are related solely to the support of our clients with catalog sales programs, and thus are exempt from the regulations most commonly associated with outbound teleservices.</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We work closely with our clients, companies we outsource outbound teleservices to and their respective advisors to ensure that we and our clients are in compliance with these regulations.&#160;&#160;We cannot predict whether the status of the regulation of outbound telephone services or e-commerce will change and what effect, if any, this change would have on us or our industry.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Mr. Hanger </font>joined Innotrac in 1994 and currently serves as Senior Vice President-Client Services.&#160;&#160;He served as a Director from December 1997 through February 2004.&#160;&#160;He served as Vice President&#8212;Business Development from November 1997 through April 1999.&#160;&#160;He served as Innotrac&#8217;s Manager of Business Development from 1994 to November 1997, and was responsible for the management of the telecommunication equipment marketing and service business.&#160;&#160;From 1979 to 1994, Mr. Hanger served as Project Manager&#8212;Third Party Marketing at BellSouth Telecommunications, Inc., a regional telecommunications company, where he managed the marketing program for BellSouth&#8217;s network services and was involved in implementing the billing options program for BellSouth with Innotrac.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Mr. Toner</font> joined Innotrac in June 2001 and currently serves as Senior Vice President<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#8212;</font>Chief Operating Officer. He held the position of Senior Vice President&#8212;Logistics from June 2001 until February 2010.&#160;&#160;Prior to joining Innotrac, Mr. Toner developed 16 years of distribution, logistics, and transportation experience; 14 of those years were with McMaster-Carr Supply Company, a distributor of industrial supplies. Subsequent to McMaster-Carr, Mr. Toner was the General Manager for East Coast Operations for Webvan Group Inc., an Internet retailer.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic">Mr. Ringer</font> joined Innotrac in 2012 and currently serves as Chief Information Officer. <div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Ms. Herren</font> has been with Innotrac since 1991 and currently serves as the Chief Accounting Officer and Corporate Controller.&#160;&#160;She also served as the company&#8217;s interim Chief Accounting Officer from January, 2005 through May, 2007.&#160;&#160;Prior to being promoted to the Corporate Controller position in November 2002, she held the Assistant Corporate Controller position from March 2000 to November 2002 and the General Accounting Manager position from March 1998 to March 2000. Ms. Herren is a certified public accountant.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 1A.&#160;&#160;RISK FACTORS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We have a large investment in fulfillment and computer technology equipment as well as long term building leases.&#160;&#160;A severe or prolonged economic downturn affecting our customers&#8217; unit volume sales could negatively impact our operating results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac provides sufficient capacity in its fulfillment operations and electronic data processing systems to allow new clients to be developed, support growth in our existing customers&#8217; business and service all customers during seasonal volume increases.&#160;&#160;The investment in that capacity can result in an underutilization in our invested assets during a significant or prolonged economic downturn.&#160;&#160;We lease our buildings with lease terms long enough to secure competitive lease rates, but which expose us to the term of the real property leases limiting our flexibility to reduce fixed capacity for periods of economic downturns.&#160;&#160;We service varied client business lines and industry verticals which provide some level of protection for such downturns.&#160;&#160;Our ability to maintain or achieve improved operating results could be partially effected by a significant multi-vertical economic downtown or the speed and strength of recovery from an economic downturn.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div id="PGBRK" style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt">
<div id="FTR">
<div id="GLFTR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>

<div id="PN" style="PAGE-BREAK-AFTER: always; WIDTH: 100%">
<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">8</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-ALIGN: center; WIDTH: 100%">
<hr style="COLOR: gainsboro" noshade size="1">
</div>
</div>

<div id="HDR">
<div id="GLHDR" style="WIDTH: 100%" align="right"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 8pt">&#160; </font></div>
</div>
</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">We rely on a small number of large clients.&#160;&#160;If we lose one or more of our largest clients, or if revenues from our largest clients decline, or if we experience unanticipated costs implementing systems and ramping up our services for new clients, our business could be adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac focuses on developing long-term contractual relationships with large corporations.&#160;&#160;A relatively small number of our clients account for a significant portion of our revenues.&#160;&#160;Our ten largest clients accounted for 76.9% of our revenue in 2012.&#160;&#160;If we lose one or more of our largest clients, or if revenues from our largest clients decline, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially adversely affected.&#160;&#160;Additionally, if one of these large clients is lost, or revenues from our largest clients decline, we cannot guarantee that we will be able to replace or supplement that client with others that generate comparable revenues or profits.&#160;&#160;Although we believe growth of our existing client base, improvement in the economic climate and continued productivity improvement would partially offset the impact of losing a large client, our future operating results would rely heavily on our ability to sell new business.&#160;&#160;Such projected new business may not develop and the future loss of any other large account could adversely affect our future results.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Noncompliance with any of the covenants under our revolving Credit Facility would allow our lender to declare any outstanding amounts to be immediately due and payable.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our Credit Facility contains financial, change of ownership control and other restrictive covenants.&#160;&#160;Noncompliance with any of the covenants would allow the lender to declare any outstanding borrowed amounts to be immediately due and payable.&#160;&#160;From time to time in the past, we have violated various restrictive covenants, and have been obligated to obtain waivers or amendments from the lender.&#160;&#160;We were in compliance with all financial covenants and other reporting requirements of the Credit Facility as of December 31, 2012 and February 28, 2013.&#160;&#160;If our operating results in the future result in our inability to comply with the existing covenants and we were unable to obtain an amendment, our credit ratings could be negatively affected impairing our ability to finance our operations which could have a material adverse effect on our financial performance and condition.&#160;&#160;The term of our Credit Facility matures on June 30, 2013.&#160;&#160;We are in discussions with several banks including our existing bank to renew the line.&#160;&#160;We are confident that a renewal of the facility will occur, but if we are unable to negotiate a renewal, our ability to finance our operations would be impaired which could have a material adverse effect on our financial performance and condition.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our written contracts generally do not guarantee specific volume levels and can usually be terminated on little notice.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Although we have written agreements with most of our clients, our agreements generally do not assure specific volume or revenue levels.&#160;&#160;In addition, some agreements provide for termination for any reason on short notice.&#160;&#160;Furthermore, we are contractually bound to our facility leases until their terms expire.&#160;&#160;If a client terminates its contract suddenly, we may still have obligations under our leases.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">If we are not able to keep pace with changing technology, our business will be materially adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our success depends significantly upon our ability to:</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#9679;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;integrate new clients in a timely and cost efficient manner;</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#9679;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;enhance existing services;</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#9679;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;develop applications to meet our clients&#8217; needs; and</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 18pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 18pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#9679;</font>&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;introduce new services and products to respond to technological developments.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">If we fail to maintain our technological capabilities or respond effectively to technological changes, our business, results of operations and financial condition could be materially adversely affected.&#160;&#160;We cannot assure you that we will select, invest in and develop new and enhanced technology on a timely basis in the future in order to meet our clients&#8217; needs and maintain competitiveness.&#160;&#160;Our Reno system, which provides service to several of our clients, is completely customized and therefore not supported by third party providers.&#160;&#160;We are heavily reliant on a small number of developers.&#160;&#160;If these developers leave, it could materially adversely affect our business.&#160;&#160;We provide details about our technology in &#8220;Business - Technology&#8221; in Item 1.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our industry is extremely competitive resulting in downward pressure on our pricing.&#160;&#160;If we cannot continue to improve our operating efficiencies, our business could be materially adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Although we continually work to improve our operating efficiencies and control selling general and administrative costs, there continue to be competitive pressures on pricing in the industry.&#160;&#160;These pressures could affect our ability to retain current customers and attract new business.&#160;&#160;If we fail to offset pricing pressures with reductions in operating costs, our business could be materially adversely affected.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Our common stock lacks liquidity and is held by a small number of investors, one of which is in receivership where its creditors would like to sell our shares as soon as possible.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As of December 31, 2012, Innotrac officers and directors owned approximately 48.2% of the outstanding common stock and an institutional shareholder, IPOF Fund, L.P., and its affiliates held approximately 32.9%.&#160;&#160;These ownership positions have resulted in a lack of liquidity in our common stock.&#160;&#160;Additionally, if any of Innotrac&#8217;s significant shareholders decided to liquidate its or their position, our common stock price would likely decline materially.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The United States District Court in Cleveland, Ohio has appointed a receiver to identify and administer the assets of the IPOF Fund, L.P. and its general partner, Mr. David Dadante.&#160;&#160;Based on information from the receiver, the Company understands that the Fund and Mr. Dadante own 4,321,777 shares of common stock of the Company, representing approximately 32.9% of the total shares outstanding, all of which are held as collateral in margin accounts maintained at several financial institutions.&#160;&#160;The Federal Court has indefinitely restricted the financial institutions holding Company stock owned by the IPOF Fund and Mr. Dadante in margin accounts from selling any of these shares.&#160;&#160;The court has permitted open market sales by the receiver as he may in his sole discretion determine to be consistent with his duty to maximize the value of the assets of IPOF Fund, and as warranted by market conditions.&#160;&#160;The receiver has indicated to the Company that he does not intend to direct any open market sales except in circumstances in which he believes that there would be no material adverse impact on the market price for the Company&#8217;s shares.&#160;&#160;Nevertheless, as long as these shares are held in margin accounts where the lenders desire to liquidate the positions, there will be significant downward pressure on the market price of our common stock because the market is concerned that these shares may be sold in a manner that causes the price of our common stock to decline precipitously.&#160;&#160;This concern is ameliorated to some degree by the prohibition by the Federal Court for an indefinite period on sales of our shares by financial institutions that hold the shares in margin accounts.&#160;&#160;The Company has engaged in discussions from time to time with the receiver in an effort to cause the shares to be sold in a manner that causes as little disruption to the market for Company stock as possible.&#160;&#160;If the Federal Court were to not continue this prohibition before the shares have been sold in such a transaction, then the financial institutions might foreclose on some or all of these shares and sell them into the market, which could have an extremely negative impact on the market price for our common stock.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">ITEM 1B.&#160;&#160;UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We are not a party to any material legal proceeding.&#160;&#160;We are, from time to time, a party to litigation arising in the normal course of our business.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;Although management believes that none of these actions, individually or in the aggregate, will have a material adverse effect on our financial position or results of operations, it is possible that such litigation and the related cost could become material in the future.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">In 2006 and 2007, certain investors in the IPOF Fund asserted claims against the Company and/or certain of its officers and directors in separate litigation actions.&#160;&#160;These actions are captioned <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Small, et al. v. Regalbuto, et al., </font>which asserts claims against the Company, and <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Amantea, et al. v. Innotrac, Inc., et al. </font>(the court docket in the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Amantea </font>action misidentifies the Company as &#8220;Innotrac, Inc.&#8221;), which asserts claims against the Company and certain current and former officers and directors of the Company, both in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.&#160;&#160;The matters were stayed by that court shortly after they were filed.&#160;&#160;In an order entered October 6, 2010, the Court dismissed the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Small, et al. v Regalbuto, et al. </font>action, without prejudice, subject to being reopened upon written motion to the Court.&#160;&#160;In an order entered November 4, 2010, the Court dismissed the <font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Amantea, et al. v. Innotrac, Inc., et al.</font> action, without prejudice, subject to being reopened upon written motion to the Court.&#160;&#160;The Court took this action because the case had been stayed for nearly three years.&#160;&#160;The Company believes the claims are without merit and would vigorously defend against these claims if they were re-filed.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Company has never declared cash dividends on the Common Stock.&#160;&#160;The Company does not anticipate paying cash dividends in the foreseeable future.&#160;&#160;Any future determination as to the payment of cash dividends will depend upon such factors as earnings, capital requirements, the Company&#8217;s financial condition, restrictions in financing agreements and other factors deemed relevant by the Board of Directors.&#160;&#160;The payment of dividends by the Company is restricted by its revolving credit facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="left"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Overview</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac, founded in 1984 and headquartered in Atlanta, Georgia, is a<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt">n e-commerce provider integrating digital technology, order processing, fulfillment and customer support <font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#8220;</font>contact<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman">&#8221;</font> center services to support global brands of large corporations that outsource these functions. </font></font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Company employs sophisticated order processing and warehouse management technology and operates eight fulfillment centers and one call center in seven cities spanning all time zones across the continental United States.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Prior to 2000, the Company was primarily focused on the telecommunications industry, with over 90% of its revenues being derived through this vertical.&#160;&#160;Today, the Company primarily serves three lines of business, or industry verticals. This is a result of a significant effort made by the Company to diversify both its industry and client base over the past several years.&#160;&#160;We classify those industry verticals as i) eCommerce/Direct to Consumer, ii) Direct Marketing, and iii) Business to Business and telecommunications.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During 2012, the company&#8217;s new business development accelerated with the addition of 10 new clients actively serviced during the year.&#160;&#160;We have expected launch dates in 2013 for serveral&#160;clients committed to using Innotrac,&#160;and we are actively pursuing other prospects.&#160;&#160;Additionally, some of our larger clients experienced an increase in volume in 2012 compared to 2011 and have indicated an expectation of continued volume growth in 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Our business has a long selling cycle.&#160;&#160;As a result of this selling cycle, new customers who committed to use Innotrac in late 2012 and early 2013 project service to begin in the late 2<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">nd</font> and 3<font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 70%; VERTICAL-ALIGN: text-top; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">rd</font> quarter of 2013.&#160;&#160;We experienced a growth of 25% in service revenues in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160;&#160;</font></div>

<div>&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Innotrac has more than twenty-seven years of experience as a provider of fulfillment services and recognizes the importance of maintaining sufficient capacity to support our clients&#8217; seasonal needs as well as allow us to grow with new clients.&#160;&#160;With no outstanding advances on our Credit Facility at December 31, 2012, we have the liquidity to increase our capacity as needed and to continue to invest in our business development activities in 2013.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Macro-Economic Factors</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During 2012, the United States economy stabilized and grew slightly following a three year negative cycle.&#160;&#160;eCommerce activity increased at a greater rate than the general economy and is expected to continue to grow in 2013, providing the potential opportunity for growth in our core business in the coming year.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We are continuing to monitor the economic trends and business experience of our customers and closely manage our operating costs which vary with volume.&#160;&#160;Additionally, we believe our mix of multiple customer industries provides some protection from the impact of the downturn as the economy recovers.&#160;&#160;However, as discussed in Item 1A &#8220;Risk Factors&#8221; of this Annual Report on Form 10-K our results can be negatively affected depending on the severity or concentration by industry of a renewed downturn.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">eCommerce/Direct-to-Consumer and Direct Marketing.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company provides a variety of services for a significant number of eCommerce, retail, and direct marketing clients which include such companies as Target.com, a division of Target Corporation, Ann Taylor Retail, Inc., Microsoft, Inc., Beachbody, LLC and Thane International.&#160;&#160;Our revenues are a result of the number of orders and customer service calls received. Our client contracts generally do not guarantee volumes.&#160;&#160;The percentage of our revenues attributable to our eCommerce and retail clients increased during 2012 as compared to 2011 as a result of the growth in their reported revenue during the same period having increased greater than our other client categories.&#160;&#160;We expect this trend to continue as we anticipate more opportunities for new business in this line and expect a higher level of organic growth than our other consumer categories.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal; TEXT-DECORATION: underline">Business to Business (B2B) and Telecomunications.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company also provides services including customer and distributor communication programs, retailer product rework/finishing services and supplier/retailer compliance reporting for business-to-business (&#8220;B2B&#8221;) clients including NAPA, The Walt Disney Company, and Spanx.&#160;&#160;The Company has historically been a major provider of fulfillment and customer support services to the telecommunications industry.&#160;&#160;Consolidation in the industry at the product supply level and changes in the technology of delivery mediums used by the telecommunications industry since 2000 has resulted in a lesser concentration of our service revenues from this industry.&#160;&#160;Accordingly, we now present our service revenue by customer vertical information with B2B services and telecommunications as a single segment.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Cost of Service Revenues.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s cost of service revenues, which include labor costs for the fulfillment and contact centers, telephone minute fees and packaging material costs, increased $10.9 million or&#160;30.1% to $47.1 million for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to $36.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Cost of service revenues as a percent of service revenues increased to 50.1% from 48.3% for the years ended December 31, 2012 and 2011, respectively.&#160;&#160;The $10.9 million increase in cost of service revenues was primarily due to the combined effect of a change in the mix of revenues by client and new customer activity using a higher percentage of temporary labor.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Freight Expense.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company&#8217;s freight expense increased $3.5 million or&#160;36.4% to $13.2 million for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to $9.6 million for the year ended December 31, 2011 due to the increase in corresponding freight revenue as discussed above.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Selling, General and Administrative Expenses.&#160;&#160;</font>S, G &amp; A expenses, which include facility and equipment costs, sales and marketing expenses, account services and information technology costs, management salaries and legal and accounting fees, increased $3.2 million or&#160;8.6% to $40.0 million or 37.1% of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to $36.8 million or 43.5 % of revenues for the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The $3.2 million increase in expenses in 2012 as compared to 2011 was primarily attributable to a i) a $1.1 million increase in facility and facility management costs due to the addition of a new facility in Ohio and facility management to support several new clients; ii.) a $379,000 increase in information technology costs due to costs related to new client implementations; and iii) a net increase in all other SG&amp;A costs of $1.7 million which includes increased sales commissions related to new clients and adjustments to the Company&#8217;s worker&#8217;s compensation claims reserve.&#160;&#160;&#160;SG&amp;A expenses as a percentage of total revenue decreased due to the growth in service revenue outpacing the increases in supporting SG&amp;A expenses.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Income Taxes.&#160;&#160;</font>The Company&#8217;s effective tax rate for the years ended 2012 and 2011 was 0%.&#160;&#160;A valuation allowance continues to be recorded against the Company&#8217;s net deferred tax assets as historical losses have created uncertainty about the realization of tax benefits in future years.&#160;&#160;Income taxes associated with the income in the year ended December 31, 2012 and the loss from the year ended December 31, 2011 were offset by a corresponding decrease or increase respectively of the valuation allowance resulting in an effective tax rate of 0% for the years ended December 31, 2012 and December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The existence of a net operating loss carryforward at December 31, 2012 means that income taxes associated with any potential taxable earnings for the year ended December 31, 2013 will be offset by a corresponding decrease of this valuation allowance, resulting in an expected effective tax rate of 0% for the year ended December 31, 2013 as well.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: bold">Liquidity and Capital Resources</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Liquidity.</font>&#160;&#160;The Company funds its operations and capital expenditures primarily through cash flow from operations and borrowings under a revolving credit facility (the &#8220;Credit Facility&#8221;) with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. (the &#8220;Bank&#8221;).</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Company had cash and cash equivalents of approximately $4.0 million at December 31, 2012 and $3.3 million at December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;Additionally, at both December 31, 2012 and 2011, the Company had no borrowings under its Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 1.8pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During the year ended December 31, 2012, the Company generated $4.9 million in cash flow from operating activities compared to generating $5.7 million cash from operating activities in the year ended December 31, 2011.&#160;&#160;The $881,000 decrease was primarily the result of the net change in all operating assets and liabilities using $2.5 million of cash for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to providing $3.8 million during the same period in 2011, offset by the Company generating a net income of $3.5 million for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to generating a net loss of $1.5 million in the same period in 2011.&#160;&#160;The $6.3 million decrease in cash provided by operating assets and liabilities for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to 2011 resulted mainly from the combined effect of i) $4.5 million decrease in cash provided by accounts receivable for the year ended December 31, 2012 compared to the same period in 2011 due to higher growth in revenue during 2012 compared to revenue growth in 2011, ii) $2.9 million greater decreases in inventory occurring in 2011 than in 2012 as a result of the end of an inventory buyback program in 2011 for a single client discussed below, and iii.) $710,000 greater decrease in long-term liabilities related to the impact of straight lining rent expense for our facilities and prepaid maintenance items, offset by a $2.0 million decrease in cash used in accounts payable and accrued expenses in 2012 compared to 2011.&#160;&#160;The $2.0 million decrease in cash used for accounts payable and accrued expenses was primarily due to an overall increase in vendor payables balance outstanding as of December 31, 2012 due to an increase in temporary employees and amounts due other suppliers to support the increased volume in 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 1.8pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">We purchase inventory for two customers under contract terms that provide that the risk of inventory obsolescence remain with our customers.&#160;&#160;During 2010, one such customer discontinued a specific business program and liquidated the inventory supporting that program.&#160;&#160;This resulted in the customer repurchasing inventory from the Company at cost.&#160;&#160;Upon buyback, there was no resulting revenue recorded in our operating results, consistent with past reporting by the Company.&#160;&#160;In the last week of March 2011, we shipped $2.9 million of inventory under normal payment terms and in mid May 2011, the resulting accounts receivable was collected from the customer.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal">During the year ended December 31, 2012, net cash used in investing activities consisted mainly of capital expenditures of $5.3 million in 2012 compared to $2.4 million in 2011.&#160;&#160;The $5.3 million of investing activities for year ended December 31, 2012 includes i) $3.3 million of purchased equipment for the build out of our new fulfillment center in Groveport, Ohio and ii) $2.0 million for all other capital expenditures.&#160;&#160;The $2.4 million of investing activities for the year ended December 31, 2011 consisted mainly of capital expenditures for all facilities which is comparable to the $2.0 million spent in 2012 for capital expenditures excluding the Groveport facility.&#160;&#160;As of December 31, 2012, the initial build out of the Groveport, Ohio facility was materially completed with the build out of the remaining 200,000 square feet of space planned for 2013 as new business needs dictate.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 1.8pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">As of December 31, 2012 and December 31, 2011, there were no net borrowings under the line of credit and $1.6 million advanced under the Equipment Loan at December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;The average daily borrowings outstanding on the Credit Facility for the year ended December 31, 2012 and 2011 were $278,000 and $304,000, respectively.&#160;&#160;The maximum borrowings outstanding on the Credit Facility for any one day during the year ended December 31, 2012 and 2011 were $2.4 million and $2.3 million, respectively.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2012 and 2011, the Company repaid $429,000 and $314,000 of principal outstanding on capital leases respectively.&#160;&#160;Additionally, during the year ended December 31, 2012 and 2011, the Company incurred $37,000 and $34,000 of loan commitment fees as a result of the Third and Second Amendments to the Credit Agreement respectively.&#160;&#160;In addition, during the year ended December 31, 2011, the Company received $17,000 from PVS related to their noncontrolling interest in Innotrac Europe.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Company generated positive cash flows from operations in 2012 and 2011.&#160;&#160;During the year ended December 31, 2012, the Company required advances followed by repayment of those advances from its Credit Facility with the Bank resulting in no amount outstanding on the Credit Facility by year end 2012 and 2011.&#160;&#160;We experienced 25% growth in service revenues in 2012 compared to 2011 and expect continued growth in service revenues in 2013.&#160;&#160;This past and anticipated growth will require us to increase our fulfillment capacity in 2013 by continuing to add equipment in the new Groveport facility and other capacity improvements in various facilities to meet our customer&#8217;s volume projections.&#160;&#160;It is estimated that $2.5 million in capital purchases will be added during 2013 to support this growth.</font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Company estimates that its cash and financing needs through 2013 will be met by its available cash at December 31, 2012, cash flows from operations, capital lease financing and availability from its Credit Facility.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt"><font style="FONT-WEIGHT: normal"><font style="FONT-STYLE: italic; DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">Credit Facilities.</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 13pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">&#160;</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">On March 27, 2009, the Company entered into the Fourth Amended and Restated Loan and Security Agreement (the &#8220;Credit Facility&#8221;) with the Bank</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">, which was subsequently amended several times.&#160;&#160;The</font><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal"> term of the Credit Facility has been extended through June 30, 2013 and the Bank maintains a security interest in all of the Company&#8217;s assets.</font></font></font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">The Credit Facility had a maximum borrowing limit of $15.0 million at both December 31, 2012 and 2011(including the issuance of letters of credit up to $2.0 million in face value), but limits borrowings to a specified percentage of eligible accounts receivable and inventory.&#160;&#160;The Credit Facility is used to fund the Company&#8217;s capital expenditures, operational working capital and seasonal working capital needs.&#160;&#160;Although total advances under the Credit Facility cannot exceed the maximum borrowing limit of $15.0 million, the Credit Facility limits borrowings at any time to a specified percentage of eligible accounts receivable and inventory, together &#8220;Eligible Collateral&#8221;, which totaled $17.8 million at December 31, 2012.&#160;&#160;The terms of the Credit Facility provide that the amount borrowed and outstanding at any time combined with certain reserves for letters of credit outstanding and general reserves be subtracted from the facility limit or the value of the total collateral to arrive at an amount of unused availability to borrow under the line of credit.&#160;&#160;The total collateral under the Credit Facility at December 31, 2012 amounted to $17.8 million, however borrowings were limited to the maximum borrowing limit of $15.0 million.&#160;&#160;There were no borrowings outstanding under the Credit Facility at December 31, 2012 and the total value of reserves and letters of credit outstanding at that date totaled $2.8 million.&#160;&#160;As a result, the Company had $12.2 million of borrowing availability under the revolving credit line at December 31, 2012.</font></div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block">&#160;</div>

<div style="TEXT-INDENT: 0pt; DISPLAY: block; MARGIN-LEFT: 0pt; MARGIN-RIGHT: 0pt" align="justify"><font style="DISPLAY: inline; FONT-FAMILY: times new roman; FONT-SIZE: 10pt; FONT-WEIGHT: normal">On March 29, 2012, the Company entered into the Third Amendment to the Credit Facility which increased the Capital Expenditure limit for 2012 to $6.0 million and provided for a $1.8 million Equipment Loan (the Equipment Loan) to partially fund the purchase of equipment for the Groveport, Ohio facility.&#160;&#160;Advances under the Equipment Loan have a five year repayment term through 60 equal $30,000 monthly payments which began on July 1, 2012.&#160;&#160;&#160;Advances under the Equipment Loan are collateralized by specifically identified fulfillment equipment as valued by an independent appraiser which is reduced by an amount equal to the monthly repayment of the Equipment.</font></div>
